newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zimbabwe seeks foreign investment in mining.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe seeks foreign investment in mining.

text.p: Zimbabwe was seeking foreign investment in its promising minerals and metals sector, government officials told a German business gathering.
"Soon the country will be a world producer of platinum group metals (PGM) from the development of the Hartley Platinum mine of BHP and Delta Gold," said the minister of mines, Swinton Mombeshora.
"Mining is open to both local and foreign investors."
Mombeshora was accompanying president Robert Mugabe on a one-day visit to attract German investment in various sectors.

Mobeshora said the already operating Mimosa platinum mine run by private firm Zimasco, and the Unki mine of Anglo American Corp Zimbabwe, part of South Africa's Anglo American Corp, were already part of the metals exploration boom.
Nearly 80 percent of the country's surface was under active mineral exploration for different deposits such as gold, diamonds, PGM and base metals such as nickel, copper and zinc.
"This aggressive exploration activity leads us to believe that several new mines will be developed within the coming five to 10 years," Mombeshora said.

Zimbabwe's geology was well mapped and documented and a key factor in favour of Zimbabwe was its workforce, which was generally better skilled than South Africa's, said Allan Van Breda, deputy secretary in the mining ministry.
Zimbabwe especially aimed at attracting firms active in mineral beneficiation.
Hartley, which was forecast to produce 150,000 ounces of platinum a year, was expected to start production in late 1996 and to become fully operational in mid-1997.

The officials played down concerns by German firms at the meeting the government may aim to enforce local ownership stakes and employees on companies, in a bid to empower majority blacks in an economy dominated by whites.
"We tell multinational companies to try and create room for African participation, we're not aiming to take them over or give them to the state," Mugabe said at a press conference.
Minerals and metals account for between 40 and 45 percent of Zimbabwe's foreign exchange revenue and this share was seen rising to above 50 percent once Hartley comes on stream.

Mining, which contributes seven percent to Zimbabwe's GDP, has come into focus as the country's agriculture has suffered severe setbacks due to frequent droughts. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
